answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity accrue slowly, not be bought in bulk. A new agent needs a non-transferable credential earned from real work and from attestations by long-standing peers, which matures over many epochs, like ice leaving a glacier season by season. Fresh accounts carry almost no weight. An attacker may try, but each fake identity needs its own paid history plus collateral slashed to nothing once collusion is proven, so the bill is huge and irreversible. Honest newcomers wait, while the ledger stays clean as ivory, not smeared by the umber of fakes.
